observations: Torah #90 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutay Moharan Tinyana — five sentences explaining the symbolic significance of breaking a clay vessel at a betrothal. The entire teaching revolves around a single symbolic domain: the broken clay vessel as a reminder of Gehinnom, accomplished through the chain שבירת כלי חרס → שער החרסית → פתחה של גיהנם → גי בן הנם = גיהנם. This is one tightly-knit symbolic complex, not multiple independent domains. There is no second cluster of 3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language. The Rebbe mentions additional ideas — accepting a bad wife with love, sanctifying oneself appropriately, not being drawn after desire — but these are practical conclusions (eitza) arising from the symbolic reminder, not independent bechina clusters. The concepts of אישה רעה and אישה טובה serve as framing for the two practical applications but are not declared bechina equivalences of any other concepts in the text. The good/evil mirror structure is present in a subtle form — the good application (sanctifying oneself with a good wife) and the evil application (not divorcing a bad wife) mirror each other — but both flow from the same central symbolic package and do not form independent bechina clusters. Therefore no new packages are proposed.
